objective.text: The purpose of this grant was to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.
objective.quote: the purpose of this grant was to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to: 1) Develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.

fuel.text: Simulations used n-heptane/air mixtures and dimethyl ether (DME) / air mixtures.
fuel.quote: (a) spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture, (b) one dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames using an arc-length continuation method and (c) simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

sample_geometry.text: The investigation maintained a one-dimensional geometry.

variables.text: A comparative study of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted.
variables.quote: a comparative studies of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted

measurements.text: The investigation aimed to obtain new, quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution.
measurements.quote: Obtain new, quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution for the validation of kinetic and radiation models involving cool flames.

earth_benefits.text: Obtaining a fundamental understanding of the warm diffusion flame is particularly relevant to combustion in highly turbulent flow fields and in microgravity environments, owing to the possibility of long residence times.
